Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 657 PM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

- The potential exists for dense fog development each of the 
daybreak periods Friday through Monday. Any fog that will develop is 
expected to dissipate or lift by 10 am.

- Mild and dry through the middle of next week.

&&

.AVIATION...

High pressure will maintain residence throughout the region this 
period as it settles into Quebec. Associated veering of wind toward 
the northeast and then east with time through Friday morning will 
set the stage for some degree of low level moisture advection off 
the upstream lakes tonight. Evidence of this already underway across 
Sagainw Bay in the form of lower stratus, suggesting a high 
likelihood for fog/low stratus expansion into portions of central 
and southeast Michigan throughout the night. Forecast will continue 
to highlight a window for IFR to LIFR conditions to emerge during 
the early morning hours. Potential does exist for a period of dense 
fog to develop, with visibility below 1/4 mile. A gradual 
improvement in conditions late morning as daytime heating works to 
lift and clear any lingering low stratus and fog. VFR conditions 
with a limited diurnal cu production for the remainder of Friday. 

D21/DTW Convection... Thunderstorms are not forecast through the TAF 
period.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Low for cigs/vsby to fall below 200 ft and/or 1/2SM.
